summary.text: Raheem Rifai is the Greens candidate for Tarneit at the 2026 Victorian election (the VEC's list gives his given names with an initial, A, first; the Greens list his family name first). A community services worker in the district for over 15 years, he has held leadership roles in local groups including the Werribee Islamic Centre, and is a union organiser who says he has signed up more than 1,600 members in tertiary education. He ran for the Greens at the Werribee by-election in February 2025, finishing with 7.6 per cent of the primary vote.

occupation.text: Community services worker and union organiser

priorities.text: More frequent and reliable bus services in Tarneit and the west
A hospital and better health facilities for Tarneit
More university and TAFE campuses in Melbourne's west

summary.text: Aijaz Moinuddin is standing as an independent for Tarneit at the 2026 Victorian state election, on the VEC's list of nominations. He founded the United People's Party, which is not registered, and has stood several times before: for Lalor at the 2019, 2022 and 2025 federal elections, for Tarneit in 2022 and at the 2025 Werribee by-election. His own campaign page says he holds a master's degree in information technology and started a software development business.

summary.text: Andrew Elsbury is The West Party's candidate for Tarneit at the 2026 Victorian election. He sat in the Legislative Council as a Liberal member for Western Metropolitan Region from 2010 until he lost his seat in 2014, and quit the Liberal Party in 2022, objecting to its shift to the right. He grew up in Hoppers Crossing, and after Parliament his jobs included corporate communications work, a stint on the electorate staff of then-MP Sarah Henderson, and project work for the Australian Industry Group.

occupation.text: Corporate communications and project work; former MP

prior_roles.role: Electorate officer to Sarah Henderson MP

priorities.text: Finishing local projects such as duplicating Sayers Road and traffic lights at Hogans and Derrimut roads
Better vocational education in the area
More police protection
Easier access to health care
An employment precinct bringing skilled jobs to Wyndham

summary.text: Dylan Wight has been the Labor member for Tarneit since the 2022 state election, when he took over the seat from Sarah Connolly as she moved to the new seat of Laverton. A former union organiser, he chaired Parliament's Electoral Matters Committee and in 2026 became parliamentary secretary for jobs and industrial relations, and later also for racing and major events. He is standing again in Tarneit in 2026.

occupation.text: Union organiser with the Australian Manufacturing Workers Union

prior_roles.role: Parliamentary Secretary for Racing and Major Events
Parliamentary Secretary for Jobs and Industrial Relations

summary.text: Horizana Niyongabire is the Family First candidate for Tarneit at the 2026 Victorian election. Her party page says she grew up in Burundi before moving to Australia, where she set up an import business dealing in international foods and products. She says she previously counselled women at her church in Adelaide. The ABC's guide listed her without a biography as at early November 2026.

occupation.text: Small business owner (food and product import business)

priorities.text: Speaking up for women and protecting children
Strengthening families
Supporting small business owners

summary.text: Leah Van Keulen is the Victorian Socialists candidate for Tarneit at the 2026 Victorian election. She has taught in Melbourne's west for nine years, is active in her union, and lives in Werribee, having spent her whole life in the western suburbs. She says Labor has treated Tarneit as a seat it can rely on, and calls for better public transport, affordable housing and more community services.

priorities.text: I believe working-class people are exploited by the existing system
Better public transport and affordable housing for Tarneit
More funding for public schools
Quality healthcare and easy access to essential services
Standing against racism and divisive politics

sources.title: Tarneit: 2026 Victorian election guide, ABC News
Leah Van Keulen, Victorian Socialists

summary.text: Maurita Rahn is the Animal Justice Party candidate for Tarneit at the 2026 Victorian election, the second time she has run for the party in this seat after 2022. She has lived in the Tarneit area for over two decades and has worked in procurement in the corrections and health sectors. She has campaigned for animal rights for 18 years and helps Victorian Dog Rescue and wildlife groups.

priorities.text: Phasing out factory farming quickly, including cages for laying hens
Pausing the proposed pet rehoming organisation scheme so rescue groups can be properly consulted
Humane alternatives to culling kangaroos trapped by development in Truganina
Ending the use of animals for entertainment, with better lifelong protection for racehorses

summary.text: Walter Villagonzalo is the One Nation candidate for Tarneit at the 2026 Victorian election. He served on Wyndham City Council between 2016 and 2020, one year of it as deputy mayor, and he received the Medal of the Order of Australia in 2025 for service to the Wyndham community. The ABC's notes say he has a military and IT background, has led a migrant support service and a multicultural business association, and has lived in the area for 38 years. He ran as an ungrouped independent for the Western Metropolitan upper house region in 2022.
